text.p: The tallest and shortest seeds in the women's singles both fell by the wayside before lunch as Wimbledon opened its doors on a Sunday for only the second time in history.

Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport and French Open semifinalist Amanda Coetzer, seeded fifth and sixth respectively, were both hustled out of the championships in straight sets and looked in danger of being joined by some other notable women's names.

While Davenport (1.89 metres) was losing 7-5 6-2 to the Czech Republic's Denisa Chladkova and Coetzer (1.52 metres) was being humiliated 6-2 6-1 by Patricia Hy-Boulais of Canada, former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez was in trouble against Helena Sukova and Monica Seles was facing an uphill struggle in her delayed second round match against Kristina Brandi.

Martinez lost the first four games of the match to Sukova and, despite fighting back to 5-4, conceded the first set 6-4. Seles, meanwhile, was poised to resume a set and 1-3 down to Brandi following men's third seed Yevgeny Kafelnikov's swift four-set win over Javier Sanchex on Centre Court.

Mary Pierce, seeded ninth, also suffered a wobble before beating Virginia Ruano Pascual 6-0 2-6 6-3. The French hope was troubled by pain in her right elbow, but kept her concentration sufficiently to set up a third round match with another Spaniard, Maria Luisa Serna.
The action was watched by an enthusiastic crowd taking advantage of the rare first come, first served ticket policy at the All England Club.
The queue of fans wishing to see some play on what is now known as "People's Sunday" was still over a mile long three hours after the gates opened at 0900 GMT.
